title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a flat, deal with the landlord, report something broken, get it fixed, sort out bills and power cuts, and get on with the neighbours.
intro:
Whether you rent a flat in Karachi's Gulshan-e-Iqbal, a portion of a house in Hyderabad's Qasimabad or a room in Sukkur, daily life at home in Sindh runs on a few conversations: with the **مالڪ** (landlord) about rent and repairs, with the plumber and electrician, with the **چوڪيدار** (watchman), and with the neighbours about noise, parking and rubbish. Add load-shedding and water tankers, and you have the vocabulary of every Sindhi household WhatsApp group.

The grammar is about **getting results**: complaining politely but firmly ('the tap has been leaking **for** three days'), asking someone to do something **for you** (ٺيڪ **ڪري ڏيو**), and the causative **ڪرائڻ** — getting something done by someone else (نل ٺيڪ **ڪرايو** 'I got the tap fixed').

grammar.title: Complaints that get results: … کان (for / since) and ڪري ڏيو (do it for me)
grammar.body:
**How long has it been going on?** English says 'the tap **has been** leaking **for** three days'. Sindhi uses the plain **present** (or the پيو continuous) with **کان** 'from' after the time — literally 'from three days the tap is leaking':

ٽن ڏينهن کان نل ليڪ پيو ٿئي — for three days
ڪالهه کان لفٽ بند آهي — since yesterday
هڪ هفتي کان گيس ڪونهي — for a week
ڪيترن ڏينهن کان؟ — for how many days?

The time word goes into the **oblique** before کان: ڏينهن → ٽن ڏينهن (ṭin ɗīṃhan), هفتو → هفتي, مهينو → مهيني. Don't use the past tense here — 'it leaked for three days' would mean it has stopped.

**Do it for me: verb + ڏيڻ.** Put the verb in its 'having done' form (ڪري, کولي, ٻڌائي…) and add **ڏيو** (polite) or **ڏي** (to a friend). It adds 'for me / for us' and sounds like a real request rather than an order: ٺيڪ ڪري ڏيو 'please fix it', در کولي ڏيو 'open the door for me', نمبر ٻڌائي ڏيو 'tell me the number'.

**Firm but polite**: start soft (معاف ڪجو، سائين…), state the problem with کان, then say what must happen with infinitive + **گهرجي** 'should, must': اهو اڄ ئي ٺيڪ ٿيڻ گهرجي 'it needs to be fixed today'. Raising your voice is a last resort — in Sindh, a polite but persistent complaint (and a phone call every day) works better.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: what you need to get done
grammar.body:
You met causatives in unit 25. Around the house, one does most of the work. When **you** do something, use ڪرڻ; when you **get someone else** to do it, use the causative **ڪرائڻ** (karāiṇu) 'to have done':

مون نل ٺيڪ ڪيو — I fixed the tap (myself)
مون نل ٺيڪ ڪرايو — I got the tap fixed

It works with every ڪرڻ expression: ٺيڪ ڪرائڻ 'get fixed', صاف ڪرائڻ 'get cleaned', مرمت ڪرائڻ 'get repaired', رنگ ڪرائڻ 'get painted'. The person who does the work takes **کان** 'by': پلمبر **کان** نل ٺيڪ ڪرايو 'I got the plumber to fix the tap'.

**Forms** (it's a regular verb with a vowel stem, like ڳالهائڻ):
Present: ڪرايان ٿو karāyāṃ tho, ڪرائي ٿو karāe tho
Past (ergative — agrees with the object): مون پکو ٺيڪ **ڪرايو** (m), مون دري ٺيڪ **ڪرائي** (f)
Future: ڪرائيندس karāīndus, ڪرائيندو karāīndo, ڪرائينداسين karāīndāsīṃ
Need to: مون کي ٺيڪ **ڪرائڻو** آهي (m object) / ٽانڪي صاف **ڪرائڻي** آهي (f object); ڪرائڻو پوندو 'will have to get done'
Requests: ڪرايو karāyo, gentle ڪرائجو karāijo

**The trap**: written Sindhi doesn't show short vowels, so ڪرايو can be **karāyo** 'got done' or **kirāyo** 'rent'. Context always decides — ڪرايو ڪيترو آهي؟ is obviously about rent!

Many other verbs have causatives in -āiṇu / -rāiṇu (you've met گهرائڻ 'to send for, order', from گهرڻ), but ڪرائڻ alone covers most of what you need around the house.

culture:
Renting in Sindh usually goes through a **property dealer** or **estate agent** (ايسٽيٽ ايجنٽ), who takes a month's rent as commission. Expect to pay two or three months' **ايڊوانس** and to sign an eleven-month **معاهدو** (agreement) on stamp paper. Landlords are often older men you address as **سائين**, **حاجي صاحب** or **چاچا**, and many repairs are negotiated, not automatic — a friendly but persistent phone call works better than an angry one.

Utilities are part of daily conversation: in Karachi the power company is K-Electric (people just say **KE**), in Hyderabad HESCO and in Sukkur SEPCO; summer **لوڊشيڊنگ** means many homes have a UPS or a generator. In much of Karachi, water arrives by **ٽينڪر**, and 'the tanker didn't come' is a real reason to be late.

Neighbours matter. New arrivals are often sent a plate of food, and you return the plate full — never empty. Call older neighbours **چاچا** / **ماسي** and those your age **ادا** / **ادي**. A building's **چوڪيدار** knows everything, and a small tip at Eid keeps the gate opening fast.

lessons.title: Finding a flat to rent

tip.title: ڪرائي تي — for rent
tip.body:
- **ڪرايو** (rent) becomes **ڪرائي** before تي: ڪرائي تي 'for rent', ڪرائي تي ڏيڻ 'to let out'.
- Ask about the **ايڊوانس** (deposit) and the **معاهدو** (agreement) before you agree.
- عمارت and لفٽ are feminine: لفٽ بند **هوندي** آهي.

tip.title: A bill "comes", and you "fill" it
tip.body:
- بل **آيو** = the bill came (in): بل ڪيترو آيو؟ 'how much was the bill?'
- بل **ڀرڻ** = to pay a bill; past: مون بل **ڀريو**.
- بجلي and گيس are feminine: بجلي **هلي وئي**، بجلي **ايندي**.
- Before ۾ or جو, -ī nouns add ءَ: **بجليءَ** جو بل، **ٽانڪيءَ** ۾.

lessons.title: Something's broken

tip.title: For three days: … کان
tip.body:
- 'It has been leaking **for** three days' = present + **کان**: ٽن ڏينهن **کان** ليڪ پيو ٿئي.
- The time word goes oblique: هفتو → هڪ هفتي کان، مهينو → مهيني کان.
- 'Do it for me' = ڪري / کولي + **ڏيو**: ٺيڪ ڪري ڏيو.

sentences.en: The fan has broken.

sentences.native: گيزر ٽن ڏينهن کان خراب آهي، پاڻي ٿڌو آهي.
sentences.roman: gīzaru ṭin ɗīṃhan khāṃ xarābu āhe, pāṇī thadho āhe.
sentences.en: The geyser's been broken for three days — the water's cold.

sentences.native: مالڪ کي ٻڌايو ته ٽانڪي ليڪ پئي ٿئي.
sentences.roman: mālika khe ɓudhāyo ta ṭānkī līk paī thie.
sentences.en: Tell the landlord the tank is leaking.

sentences.native: مرمت ڪڏهن ٿيندي؟
sentences.roman: maramata kaɗahiṃ thīndī?
sentences.en: When will the repair be done?

sentences.native: در کولي ڏيو، مان ٻاهر آهيان.
sentences.roman: daru kholī ɗiyo, māṃ ɓāhari āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: Open the door for me, I'm outside.

sentences.native: هڪ مهيني کان مرمت جو انتظار پيا ڪريون.
sentences.roman: hika mahīne khāṃ maramata jo intizāru pyā karyūṃ.
sentences.en: We've been waiting a month for the repair.

sentences.native: نل اڄ ئي ٺيڪ ٿيڻ گهرجي.
sentences.roman: nalu aʄu ī ṭhīku thiyaṇu ghurje.
sentences.en: The tap needs to be fixed today.

lessons.title: Getting it fixed

tip.title: ڪرائڻ — get it done
tip.body:
- ڪرڻ = do it yourself; **ڪرائڻ** = get someone to do it: نل ٺيڪ **ڪرايو** 'I got the tap fixed'.
- The worker takes **کان**: پلمبر **کان**.
- Past agrees with the thing: پکو **ڪرايو**، دري **ڪرائي**.
- Need to: ٺيڪ **ڪرائڻو** آهي (m) / **ڪرائڻي** (f).

new: مون کي نل ٺيڪ ڪرائڻو آهي.
ڪنهن سٺي پلمبر جو نمبر آهي؟

sentences.native: مون اليڪٽريشن کان پکو ٺيڪ ڪرايو.
sentences.roman: moṃ elekṭrīshana khāṃ pakho ṭhīku karāyo.
sentences.en: I got the electrician to fix the fan.

sentences.native: مون دري ٺيڪ ڪرائي.
sentences.roman: moṃ darī ṭhīku karāī.
sentences.en: I got the window fixed.

sentences.native: اسان رڌڻو رنگ ڪرايو.
sentences.roman: asāṃ radhaṇo rangu karāyo.
sentences.en: We had the kitchen painted.

sentences.native: پلمبر کان نل ٺيڪ ڪرايو؟
sentences.roman: plambara khāṃ nalu ṭhīku karāyo?
sentences.en: Did you get the plumber to fix the tap?

sentences.native: توهان کي ٽانڪي صاف ڪرائڻي پوندي.
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ khe ṭānkī sāfu karāiṇī pavandī.
sentences.en: You'll have to get the tank cleaned.

sentences.native: اسان کي هر سال ٽانڪي صاف ڪرائڻي پوي ٿي.
sentences.roman: asāṃ khe har sāla ṭānkī sāfu karāiṇī pave thī.
sentences.en: We have to get the tank cleaned every year.

sentences.native: مالڪ چوي ٿو ته پاڻ ٺيڪ ڪرائيندو.
sentences.roman: māliku chave tho ta pāṇa ṭhīku karāīndo.
sentences.en: The landlord says he'll get it fixed himself.

sentences.native: پلمبر سڀاڻي ڏهين وڳي ايندو.
sentences.roman: plambaru subhāṇe ɗahīṃ vaɠe endo.
sentences.en: The plumber's coming tomorrow at ten.

sentences.native: مرمت جو خرچ ڪير ڏيندو؟
sentences.roman: maramata jo xarchu ker ɗīndo?
sentences.en: Who will pay for the repairs?

sentences.native: اليڪٽريشن ڪيترا پئسا ورتا؟
sentences.roman: elekṭrīshana ketirā paisā vartā?
sentences.en: How much did the electrician charge?

sentences.native: مان سومر تي در جي مرمت ڪرائيندس.
sentences.roman: māṃ sūmara te dara jī maramata karāīndus.
sentences.en: I'll get the door repaired on Monday. (man)

lessons.title: Getting on with the neighbours

tip.title: Complaining to a neighbour, nicely
tip.body:
- Open softly: **ادا / ادي، معاف ڪجو…**
- Ask with the gentle **-jo** form and **ٿورو**: ٿورو آواز گهٽ **ڪجو**.
- مٿي وارا = the people upstairs; ڪچري وارو = the rubbish man.
- To say they bother you: اسان **کي** تنگ ڪن ٿا.

new: توهان جي گاڏي منهنجي در جي اڳيان بيٺي آهي.

sentences.native: اسان جو پاڙو ڏاڍو سٺو آهي.
sentences.roman: asāṃ jo pāṛo ɗāḍho suṭho āhe.
sentences.en: Our neighbourhood is really nice.

sentences.native: ادا، معاف ڪجو، ٻار ڏاڍو شور پيا ڪن.
sentences.roman: adā, māf kajo, ɓāra ɗāḍho shoru pyā kan.
sentences.en: Excuse me, brother — the kids are making a lot of noise.

sentences.native: ادي، ٽي وي جو آواز ٿورو گهٽ ڪجو.
sentences.roman: adī, ṭī vī jo āvāzu thoro ghaṭu kajo.
sentences.en: Sister, could you turn the TV down a little?

sentences.native: چوڪيدار رات جو در بند ڪري ٿو.
sentences.roman: chaukīdāru rāti jo daru bandu kare tho.
sentences.en: The watchman locks the gate at night.

sentences.native: چوڪيدار کي چئو ته ڪچرو کڻي وڃي.
sentences.roman: chaukīdāra khe chao ta kachiro khaṇī vañe.
sentences.en: Ask the watchman to take the rubbish away.

sentences.native: ڪچرو گهٽيءَ ۾ نه رکو.
sentences.roman: kachiro ghiṭīa meṃ na rakho.
sentences.en: Please don't leave rubbish in the street.

sentences.native: هتي پارڪنگ جي جاءِ ڪونهي.
sentences.roman: hite pārkinga jī jāi konhe.
sentences.en: There's no parking space here.

sentences.native: توهان جي ڪار منهنجي پارڪنگ ۾ آهي.
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ jī kāra munhinjī pārkinga meṃ āhe.
sentences.en: Your car is in my parking space.

sentences.native: هو پاڙيسري اسان کي ڏاڍو تنگ ڪن ٿا.
sentences.roman: hū pāṛesirī asāṃ khe ɗāḍho tangu kan thā.
sentences.en: Those neighbours really bother us.

sentences.native: معاف ڪجو، توهان کي تنگ ڪيو.
sentences.roman: māf kajo, tavhāṃ khe tangu kayo.
sentences.en: Sorry to bother you.

lessons.title: Moving in, moving out
new: اسين ايندڙ مهيني شفٽ ٿي رهيا آهيون.
السلام عليڪم، اسين نوان پاڙيسري آهيون.

sentences.native: اسين گلشن ۾ شفٽ ٿي رهيا آهيون.
sentences.roman: asīṃ gulshan meṃ shifṭ thī rahyā āhyūṃ.
sentences.en: We're moving to Gulshan.

sentences.native: توهان ڪڏهن شفٽ ٿيا؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ kaɗahiṃ shifṭ thiyā?
sentences.en: When did you move in?

sentences.native: اسين گذريل هفتي شفٽ ٿياسين.
sentences.roman: asīṃ guzriyala hafte shifṭ thiyāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We moved last week.

sentences.native: سامان هن پيٽيءَ ۾ رکو.
sentences.roman: sāmānu hin peṭīa meṃ rakho.
sentences.en: Put the things in this box.

sentences.native: مٿي واري فليٽ ۾ ڪير رهي ٿو؟
sentences.roman: mathe vāre flaiṭa meṃ ker rahe tho?
sentences.en: Who lives in the flat upstairs?

sentences.native: پيٽيون ڳريون آهن، مٿي کڻي هلو.
sentences.roman: peṭyūṃ ɠaryūṃ āhin, mathe khaṇī halo.
sentences.en: The boxes are heavy — carry them upstairs.

sentences.native: ڪا تڪليف هجي ته ٻڌائجو.
sentences.roman: kā takalīfa huje ta ɓudhāijo.
sentences.en: If you need anything, do let us know.

sentences.native: شفٽ ٿيڻ ۾ ٻه ڏينهن لڳندا.
sentences.roman: shifṭ thiyaṇa meṃ ɓa ɗīṃha laɠandā.
sentences.en: Moving will take two days.

sentences.native: نوان پاڙيسري ڪير آهن؟
sentences.roman: navāṃ pāṛesirī ker āhin?
sentences.en: Who are the new neighbours?

sentences.native: مالڪ اڃا ايڊوانس واپس نه ڪيو آهي.
sentences.roman: mālika añā eḍvānsu vāpasi na kayo āhe.
sentences.en: The landlord still hasn't given back the deposit.
